Read in Data

obj <- readRDS('~/Desktop/optimal_clustering_rna_only.rds')
obj_6_only = subset(obj, final_clusters == 6)
  expr_matrix <- obj_6_only@assays$RNA$data

Ok here is the situation. I have the theory that new cells are added to cluster 6 in the intermediate state and then mature during gonadal sex change (or something like that, the point is the main changes in the neurosecretory preoptic area are set up prior to gonadal sex change but only actually occur during gonadal sex cahnge). This is supported by a few lines of evidence

CytoTRACE shows that intermediates have significantly more immature cells than females, but no difference to males

Sox2 (a stem cell marker) is expanded in intermediates, the proportion of cells expressing it is larger

The population of 6_NPO increases in females late in sex change

Coltan showed new cells are added to the aPOA in intermediates

Radial glia show a more neurogenic signature in intermediates (neural progenitors are expanded while stem cells are contracted, and transcription factors also change in an interesting way)

From this, I would hypothesize that in intermediates, there would be more expression of genes related to - Synaptogenesis - Axonogenesis - Neuronal Differentiation - Neuronal Maturation - Extracellular Matrix

SO, I thought why not make an expression module of genes annotated with those GO terms and see if the modules differ in expression

To do this, I translate the GO terms from the human genome to the ortholog in A. ocellaris (A ocellaris genome doesnt have as good annotations). Then, calculate a module score with AUCell (very similar results to taking the first principal component of those genes’ expression), then I run lm(mean_module ~ Status) and get the type III p value using anova(model, test = ‘Chisq’).

The problem: I see very consistent results and they are very interesting, and yet I am basically incapable of getting a significant p- value. Broadly, mixed and fixed models return very similar p-values.

Here are my examples below

+Stem cell differentiation. Hypothesis: no difference, there shouldn’t be stem cells in 6

plot_go_aucell('GO:0048863', obj_6_only)+
  labs (title='stem cell differentiation')

Almost but not significant, honestly shocked at how much of a difference there is

model_go_aucell('GO:0048863', obj_6_only) %>%anova(test= 'Chisq') #0.07

So to me at least it seems like a pretty consistent theme is that intermediates have a notably higher expression of genes related to like new immature neurons integrating and becoming functional (synaptogenesis, axonogenesis, neuron projection development, as well as the opposite pattern of neuron maturation), and no difference in neurogenesis terms which makes sense to me cause that shoud be happening in radial glia. All but one of these terms do not significantly differ by phase. Its impressive, I’ve done enough tests that we are entering the 5% false positive rate of these models. Looking at all of these though, it seems like there is a lot of evidence that intermediates have more immature neurons than males or females, but only one GO term reaches the significance threshold. I am not really sure what to do here. A few ideas 1) we just report a few of the interesting ones and say “its not significant but like look at it its interesting”. 2) We could report a lot of these with a lollipop plot that reports how much greater the marginal estimate for intermediates is compared to males and females. 3) We could summarize a lot of these with PCA and that might then become significant. The problem with that last one (because I already tried it) is twofold. 1) You have to pick a broad go term (I tried brain development) and then do the PCA based on all of the offspring terms so as not to pick and choose your data (in my opinion, though you may disagree). This kind of destroys any result with noise. 2) GO modules are not all made the same, each one is made of a different number of genes. Should we weight a module of 2 genes the same as a module of 100 genes, I am not convinced we should.

What would you do in this situation
